newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on weather and technicals.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on weather and technicals.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on Midwest weather that was less threatening to the crop than earlier expected plus a technical slip, traders said.

"They couldn't rally it early so the ones that bought it early sold out. They got discouraged and bailed out and some of the weathermen were warmer in their midday updates," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

"The market's trying to get off dead center but hasn't done it yet," a trader said. Traders said the market showed little reaction to a Farmers Commodities Corp forecast of 1996 U.S. corn production at 9.078 billion bushels.
"I think we're trading a nine to 9.1 number now," a trader said.

The weather provided mixed signals. Bulls cited freezing temperatures in the northern portion of the growing region as possibly harming the crop, but bears said the freeze line did not extend far enough south to do much damage.
Nearby December corn touched a session low of $2.91-1/2, the lowest level for that month since $2.88-1/2 was reached on January 26.
Corn futures closed 1-1/2 cents per bushe lower to 2-1/2 higher, with December down 3/4 at $2.92.
Technicians cited support in the December at $2.89-3/4 and again at $2.81-1/2.
The nine-day relative strength index for December closed at 13.6, well below the 20 level an area generally considered indicative of an oversold market.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 50,000, down from 72,067 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Rosenthal Collins bought 1,000 December $3.10 puts at 19-1/2 cents, the traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 26,000, down from 33,959 Wednesday.
